solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decrepit folk making pots

explanation.surface: Frail old people still turning out pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Crock is both a word for a broken-down old person and for an earthenware pot.

clue.text: Bring back shop, needing engineers first

indicators.note: first says the engineers come before the shop

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Reopen the shop, but get the engineers in beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to a former state or place.

clue.text: Does trade reportedly in these small rooms

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: to do trade is to sell, so does trade means sells

explanation.surface: Business is said to be done in these little rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Cells are small compartments or rooms, as in a prison or monastery.

clue.text: Animated little man's given external support during ride

indicators.note: the little man is given something placed outside him, so it wraps around his letters

parts.note: a stirrup supports a rider's foot on horseback
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A small chap gets roused up with a foot-hold while riding.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed goes inside STIRRUP, between the R and the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred up means excited, agitated or roused, as an animated crowd is.

clue.text: New protection for the thing brought back, withdrawn

indicators.note: a protective cover wraps around what it guards, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: new means recent

indicators.note: brought back says the word for the thing is read backwards

parts.note: the thing is it

explanation.surface: A fresh covering for something returned is kept out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective on 'protection', but it gives the outer word; 'protection for' is the container signal and 'brought back' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and uncommunicative, which is what withdrawn means of character.

clue.text: Rule with rod of iron concerning journalists

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A tyrant's dealings with reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to subdue or keep down by force, ruling harshly.

clue.text: Pound pocketed by uncouth robber

indicators.note: pocketed by says the letters are tucked away inside the following words

explanation.surface: Money stolen by a rough thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money pocketed by a thief; here it is a verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat or pulsate heavily, as to pound does.

clue.text: Girl in cold and desolate area to north where kids are kept in

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a lass is a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a moor is a bleak open upland

explanation.surface: A girl in a chilly bleak place up north where children are confined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just joins the pieces. Kids are kept in a classroom, or kept in after school.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom is where pupils are taught and, in detention, kept in.

clue.text: Phone school up — not a lengthy communication

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the pieces read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: tel is the abbreviation for telephone
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: Calling the school with only a brief message.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for a short letter or message.

clue.text: Arrogant film star, 'pet' with no fans

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A conceited movie star treated as a darling, yet with no admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like admirers but is the anagram signal; 'with' just joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-important has an exaggerated sense of their own worth, i.e. is haughty and arrogant.

clue.text: Understand prisoner's genuine

parts.note: a con is a convict, so prisoner's gives con's
genuine means true

explanation.surface: Seeing the inmate is telling the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret or take a meaning from words, i.e. to understand them.

clue.text: It sounds like public vehicle will hurry along

indicators.note: the clue openly says the letters are what a phrase is heard as

parts.note: a bus is a public vehicle, and will contracts to 'll, so the phrase is bus'll

explanation.surface: A remark that the bus is about to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bustle is to move about hurriedly and energetically.

clue.text: Furious ambassador confronts an old rocker

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
an gives the article a
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll

explanation.surface: An angry diplomat squares up to an ageing rock fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronts' just puts the ambassador first. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who followed rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated argument or person is hot with anger, close to furious.

clue.text: Delight in aircraft, say

definitions.meaning: a state of rapture or ecstasy
aircraft are an example of a means of conveyance

explanation.surface: Joy in a plane, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport means both ecstasy and vehicles that carry people, such as aircraft.

clue.text: Yells about backward-looking union — they deny opportunities for some of the players

definitions.text: they deny opportunities for some of the players

indicators.note: about means around, so the yells word goes round the other piece

parts.note: yells means shouts

indicators.note: backward-looking says the union abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: TU is a trade union

explanation.surface: Cries against a reactionary trade union that is shutting players out.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, shutouts are games in which one side is kept from scoring at all.

clue.text: Endeavour to make provision for someone who is late?

definitions.meaning: to attempt or take on a task

definitions.text: make provision for someone who is late?
definitions.meaning: an ... arranges funerals for the deceased, the late

explanation.surface: Trying to make arrangements for a person who is running behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy but means dead: the second sense plays on the funeral undertaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake is to commit to a task; the undertaker provides for the dead.

clue.text: Street entertainer, a big fellow

parts.note: a rapper is a performer of rap music

explanation.surface: A busker in the road who is a hefty man.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapper is an informal word for a tall, robust, strongly built person.

clue.text: Little piggy swallowing sparkling drink and hot snack

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the piggy wraps around the drink

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy' each piggy is a toe
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A little pig gulping fizz and a warm bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a hot snack.

clue.text: One church among others with most in the collection plate?

definitions.text: with most in the collection plate?

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the rest goes around the other letters

parts.note: the rest means the others
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single congregation among many gives the biggest offering.
explanation.definitionFit: The richest has most money, playfully pictured as having the most in the church collection.

clue.text: Maiden is overwhelmed by river, resulting in this?

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by water is engulfed, so the river goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman swept away by a river, with death as the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole picture: a maiden engulfed by a river ends in her death.
explanation.definitionFit: Demise is a formal word for death, the result of being drowned.

clue.text: Boys collecting pence, needing men who may give financial support?

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the boys word goes around the coin

parts.note: sons are boys
OR, other ranks, is soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Lads gathering coins but needing grown-ups to back them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' just joins the pieces. The picture is a sponsored event.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is one who backs a person or event with money.

clue.text: One American state or another lacking a river

indicators.note: lacking says letters are taken away from the other state

parts.note: Arkansas is another US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two US states compared, one of them short of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a state in the central United States.

clue.text: Fur OK for use but not correct for top people

indicators.note: but not says a letter is taken away from the first word

parts.note: usable means fit for use
U is old British shorthand for upper-class usage, what the top people deem correct

explanation.surface: Usable fur, though not quite the done thing for the upper crust.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels popularised in 1950s Britain for upper-class and non-upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the prized dark fur of a small Asian marten-like animal.

clue.text: Naughty man (or 'cad') offers spice

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved rogue presents a flavouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom, also spelt cardamon, is an aromatic spice from seeds of a ginger-family plant.

clue.text: Expert departs within a short time

indicators.note: within says the departs abbreviation is set inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
short says time is cut to its abbreviation T
dep is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A skilled person leaves almost at once.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is someone highly skilled, a master or expert.

clue.text: Mob talker sure excited folk looking to make mischief

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser surely stirring up a crowd of agitators.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublemakers are people who deliberately cause difficulty or mischief.

clue.text: Feeling ecstatic, one assigned to part of hospital

parts.note: sent is old slang for transported with delight
one is the Roman numeral I
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Thrilled to be posted to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive or feel things.

clue.text: Teresa cooked apples

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or messed with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teresa baked some apples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' points the wrong way: eaters are dessert apples, the ones not meant for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaters are apples grown for eating raw rather than cooking.
